newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada okays Shaw satellite TV service.
newsitem.headline: Canada okays Shaw satellite TV service.

text.p: The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) said on Friday it approved an application by Shaw Communications Inc to operate a national satellite TV distribution service called Homestar.
Homestar, a direct-to-home (DTH) service, will be owned and operated by Shaw, but will be separate from the company's cable business.
"The structural separation between Homestar and Shaw cable operations...will ensure fair competition in the DTH market," the CRTC said in statement.

Shaw is the fourth Canadian company to get a DTH license. The others were ExpressVu -- owned by BCE Inc's, Tee-Comm Electronics Inc, Canadian Satellite Communications Inc (Cancom) and WIC Western International Communications Ltd -- Power Corp of Canada's Power DirecTV, and Star Choice. All four licenses expire in 2002.
"Given the current shortage of Canadian satellite capacity, several alternative satellite strategies have been identified to deliver the Homestar service," the CRTC said.
Canada has set a February 28 deadline for Canadian satellite operators to apply for licenses to operate two vacant Canadian satellite slots.
Tee-Comm said last August that it had filed an application with the CRTC to operate its own DTH service.
